svg.title: OSDU Delivery: System Context diagram for OSDU Delivery
svg.desc: Source data comes in on the left and leaves as OSDU records on the right; the people who build and run the estate are above, the systems it relies on below.
svg.text: System Context diagram for OSDU Delivery
Source data comes in on the left and leaves as OSDU records on the right; the people who build and run the estate are above, the systems it relies on below.

g.title: Estate repository: The estate as YAML and JSON files in git: flows, mappings, templates, cache definitions, schedules, assertions and AI contexts. A run executes the commit the control plane last synced, never a working copy.
g.text: The estate as files: flows, mappings,
What runs is the commit last synced.

g.title: Pipeline developer: Writes the estate's flows, mappings, templates, schedules, assertions and AI contexts in VS Code, checks and previews them against the synced estate, and pushes them to the estate repository.

Data operator: Triggers and watches runs, follows a record from its source file and row to the OSDU id and version it landed as, releases, redelivers or removes records, reads assertion reports and asks the assistant.
g.text: follows a record from its source
row to OSDU, and acts on it.

g.title: Administrator: Registers and describes OSDU partitions, sets the central configuration every run resolves with, approves AI contexts, manages users and sets retention on the Maintenance page.

AI coding assistants: An assistant a person runs (Claude Code, the VS Code chat, Cursor, Codex). It calls the MCP server with the person's own token, so it can do what that person can do, and what it does is recorded as theirs.
g.text: Claude Code, the VS Code chat, Cursor or
Codex: a person's own assistant, reading

g.title: Source systems: Where the data starts. Upstream applications and jobs drop files (CSV, JSON, Parquet, LAS and others) into the landing storage, or hold the data in a database a flow reads.
g.text: Upstream applications and jobs that drop
subsurface data as files, or hold it in

g.title: OSDU Delivery: SQLFlow with the OSDU module installed: SQLFlow lands and keys the source data; the module renders each row through its mapping, delivers it to OSDU and keeps the ledger, from which every delivered record can be reconstructed.
g.text: Publishes subsurface records into an OSDU platform and keeps a ledger
that traces each one to its source row, its rendering and every attempt.

g.title: OSDU data platform: A data partition's core services (Storage, Search, Schema, Legal, File, Dataset, Workflow, Entitlements) and its domain data management services (Wellbore, Reservoir over ETP, Production), which hold the delivered records and their bulk data.
g.text: The target partition: its core services and
(DDMS) that hold records and bulk data.

g.title: Microsoft Entra ID: Signs people in to the GUI, the editor and the command line (OpenID Connect) through the app registration's one role, SqlFlow.User, with assignment required, and issues the managed identity and client-credential tokens (OAuth 2.0) the services use for Azure and OSDU.
g.text: Signs people in through the app role
SqlFlow.User, and issues the tokens the services

g.title: AI model provider: The chat model behind the GUI assistant and Explain: a Foundry deployment (gpt-5.1 in the shipped environments), or OpenAI or Anthropic by setting, plus an optional transcription deployment for voice. Off on a fresh deployment; no flow, mapping, render or delivery ever calls a model.
g.text: Answers the assistant's questions: gpt-5.1 on Azure AI
Foundry by default, or OpenAI or Anthropic. No flow

svg.text: Icon: what it is, or its Azure service
Calls or serves an AI model
Has a view of its inside
